CIBC slashes gold price forecasts but sees recovery to $5,200 in 2027 as central bank demand offsets Fed headwinds
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold prices remain stuck in neutral, clinging to support around $4,100 an ounce as inflation pressures drive bond yields and the U.S. dollar higher; however, one Canadian bank remains bullish on the precious metal over the longer term, even as it significantly lowers its price forecasts through the end of the decade. In its latest precious metals outlook, commodity analysts at CIBC Capital Markets lowered their fourth-quarter gold price forecast to $4,500 an ounce, down 31% from their $6,500 estimate from the start of the year. The bank now expects gold prices to average $5,200 an ounce in 2027, down from its previous forecast of $6,500, and $5,500 in 2028, compared with its earlier estimate of $6,000. Long-term, the bank expects gold prices to average $4,800 an ounce in 2029, $4,500 in 2030 and $4,200 in 2031. Commodity analysts led by Anita Soni and Cosmos Chiu said that although the monetary policy environment has become increasingly challenging for gold , the fundamental drivers that supported last year's historic rally remain firmly in place.

items.titleEn: Gold struggling to catch a bid even as U.S. pending home sales drop 7.3%
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market continues to struggle to attract any safe-haven demand, even as the U.S. housing market continues to lose significant momentum, with the number of Americans planning to buy a home dropping sharply in September. The U.S. pending home sales index dropped 7.3 in last month, the NAR announced on Tuesday. The data was significantly worse than forecasts, as economists expected only a 0.6% decline. The NAR said that weakness in the housing sector is broad-based, with all regions reporting monthly and annual declines.

Gold weaker, silver mixed as weak housing data offsets rising oil prices - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) – Spot gold prices were lower and spot silver prices were volatile in early U.S. trading Tuesday, as weaker-than-expected housing activity highlighted the impact of elevated borrowing costs on the U.S. economy, while rising crude oil prices and persistent inflation continued to support expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening. The latest housing figures provided some counterweight to the inflation concerns weighing on precious metals, although renewed tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz limited the scope for interest rate relief. In early morning trading, spot gold was near $4,120.10 an ounce, down 0.48%, while spot silver was near $57.210, up 0.42%. U.S. housing construction weakened in September, adding to evidence that elevated mortgage rates are restraining residential investment. Housing starts fell 5.2% to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.221 million units, compared with an upwardly revised 1.288 million in August . Starts were 7.4% below their year-earlier level. Single-family construction declined 4.6% to an annual rate of 859,000 units, while building permits edged down 0.2% to 1.400 million units from a revised 1.403 million in August. Single-family permits dropped 4.0% to 845,000 units. The weakness followed Monday's decline in the NAHB housing market index to 29 from 32, its lowest reading since June 2012, as rising mortgage rates, construction costs and weakening buyer traffic weighed on builders' confidence. The latest figures reinforce concerns that restrictive financial conditions are increasingly affecting interest rate-sensitive sectors of the economy.

items.titleEn: ‘Short the dollar' and hold gold or Bitcoin as inflation erodes wealth – Ledn's Reeds
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Inflation and jurisdictional risks are serving as powerful examples of the value of alternative assets like gold and Bitcoin , and the ability to borrow against these non-yielding assets could make them even more attractive in the coming years, according to Adam Reeds, CEO of digital-asset-backed lending platform Ledn – which is launching Tether Gold-backed loans in the coming weeks. Reeds said that since COVID, not only seasoned investors but also average people have been enrolled in a crash course on the impacts of inflation on prices and on wealth preservation. “Everyone, including those who are far from being sophisticated investors, is talking about inflation and how to combat it,” he said. The investing community is obviously a section of that. But it's interesting to see how important that is for everyday people as well.”

Spot gold price near low after U.S. housing starts fall 5.2%, building permits fall 0.2% in September
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold prices are trading near session lows this morning after the latest data showed the U.S. housing market delivering a weaker-than-expected performance last month. Housing starts fell 5.2% in September to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.221 million units, the Commerce Department announced on Tuesday. The data was worse than expected as economists looked for a print of 1.300 million units. August’s number was revised up to 1.288 million units. The report said that building permits for future homebuilding fell 0.2% to a rate of 1.400 million in September, which was better than the consensus expectation for 1.390 million permits, while August's figure was unrevised at 1.403 million.
